subject: Emerald - latency-tail and dedicated slab recommendation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Emerald - latency-tail and dedicated slab recommendation

Jason / ops team —

Thanks again for sharing the traffic samples. We pulled the CSV and ran a quick sensitivity pass to translate your user traffic into tokens/sec and expected GPU footprint for a production Dedicated slab. High-level assumptions we used (details attached in emerald_sla_sensitivity_v2.xlsx):

- Model target: open-13B baseline (quantized FP16/4) for parity with your evals.
- Typical tokens per response: 120 tokens (median), 320 tokens (95th percentile)
- Peak concurrent requests: 240 concurrent sessions (observed demo-day spikes at ~1.2x baseline)
- Target SLO: 95% of responses under 450 ms p95 latency (end-to-end generation time)

Quick numbers:
- Baseline peak RPS estimate: 240 concurrent * 0.8 RPS = 192 RPS (we use 0.8 RPS to reflect user think-time patterns)
- Tokens/sec (p50): 192 * 120 = 23,040 tokens/sec
- Tokens/sec (p95 bursts): 192 * 320 = 61,440 tokens/sec

Inference footprint / slab sizing note: a single H100 80GB in our runtime (with the above model and batching tuned for low-latency interactive SLOs) sustains roughly 8k–10k tokens/sec for p50 workloads and ~4k–5k tokens/sec when you need tight p95 latency under 450 ms with KV cache misses. For planning we recommend sizing to p95-burst requirements plus headroom.

Early recommendation (sustained + burst):
- Sustained capacity: 6x H100 to cover steady p95-like load (~6 * 9k ≈ 54k tokens/sec achievable with conservative kernel choices, batching limits, and prefix caching)
- Burst cushion: an additional 2x H100 or a reserved burst pool (total committed 8x H100) to absorb demo spikes and avoid falling back to hosted variants

Fallback plan: if cost or procurement prefers an A100 footprint, expect ~30–40% more GPUs to hit the same p95 headroom (so ~10–11x A100 equivalent). We included both H100 and A100 options in the attached proposal.

Next steps: Ben and Laura — can you review the attached sensitivity workbook and confirm the per-GPU throughput numbers we should lock into the proposal? Jason — if you agree with the approach I’ll attach a formal commitment sketch + DocuSign and we can schedule the capacity cutover window the week after signature.

Thanks,

Priyom — quick compute pass and clarifications below. I used the sample traces you sent and simulated request batching latency curves with our 13B config. Key technical notes: 

1) Assumptions we validated from the trace:
   - Effective RPS at peak: 190–200 RPS (matches your 192 estimate)
   - Token distribution: mean 110, p95 310 (we rounded to your conservative 120/320 for proposal)

2) Modeling approach: we calculate tokens/sec demand and map to per-GPU sustained throughput (measured from our internal benchmark harness for the exact model+quantization):
   - Per-H100 conservative sustained (interactive SLO): 9,000 tokens/sec
   - Per-H100 p95-burst capacity (short-window, low-batching): 5,500 tokens/sec
   - Per-A100 conservative sustained: 6,200 tokens/sec

3) Capacity math (p95 safety):
   - p95 burst demand: 61,440 tokens/sec (from Priyom)
   - If we size to H100 p95-burst: required = ceil(61,440 / 5,500) = 12 H100 (this is strict p95 sizing without batching benefits)
   - If we leverage Autoscale + short burst pool + prefix caching we can meet the same SLO with committed 6 H100 + 2 H100 burst (8 total), provided we accept a short warmup to bring extra replicas online for longer bursts >30s

4) Operational recommendations:
   - Commit 6x H100 as the baseline reserved slab for steady-state plus predictable headroom for common peaks.
   - Add a reserved burst pool of 2x H100 that can be routed when telemetry indicates sustained >40k tokens/sec for >20s.
   - Use aggressive prefix/KV caching and model compilation tuned to your 95th percentile sequence length to retain latency SLO.
   - Canary the rollout with 1 H100 and traffic split 90/10 for 48 hours before flipping 100% routing.

Cost vs. strict p95 tradeoff: strict p95 sizing (12x H100) is expensive and often unnecessary when you have burst-buffers + graceful fallback to a slightly cheaper quantized variant. We included a variant line-item in the PDF showing the 12x H100 worst-case vs 8x H100 (commit + burst) and the expected delta in monthly spend.

I’ve annotated the spreadsheet with the per-GPU throughput tests (tab: bench-results). Laura — please sanity-check ops/runbook items and SLA language in the proposal PDF before we send.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Thanks Priyom / Ben — this is helpful. A few questions from procurement / infra side before we can sign: 

- Can you break out the monthly committed cost for the 6xH100 + 2x burst pool vs. the strict 12x H100? We need both numbers for our finance deck.
- For the burst pool: how fast can those 2x H100 be cold-started and routed under your standard Private plan? We have short demo spikes that occasionally last 60–90s.
- Can we opt for a mixed slab (4x H100 + 4x A100) to reduce capex while still meeting p95 with some additional autoscale? If so, please include performance parity assumptions.

Also attaching a short procurement checklist that lists our internal approvals and contract milestones. We’d like the DocuSign sketch and a cost worksheet before the exec review next Wednesday.

—Jason

Jason — thanks, noted. Short answers and next steps below: 

1) Costs (high-level): we’ll send a line-item cost worksheet in the proposal PDF but ballpark monthly committed costs:
   - 6x H100 committed + 2x burst pool (reserved) ≈ $1,020,000 / month (includes support, networking, and reserved hot spares)
   - Strict 12x H100 (no autoscale or burst) ≈ $1,760,000 / month
   - Mixed (4x H100 + 4x A100 + autoscale) ≈ $1,120,000 / month (savings vs 6x H100 are modest once you account for A100 lower throughput and extra ops overhead)

2) Cold-start timing for burst pool: under our Private plan the reserved burst instances are pre-warmed (image & model cached) and can be wholly routed within 18–35s depending on concurrent topology; if you rely on autoscale from zero it can be 90–180s so we recommend reserved burst for demo-day guarantees.

3) Mixed slab viability: yes, a mixed slab is possible. Expect to provision ~30–40% more A100 capacity to match H100 steady-state throughput. We’ll include a per-GPU assumption table in the worksheet.

Attached: proposal-emerald-dedicated.pdf (includes full cost worksheet, SLA wording, rollout plan, and DocuSign link).
